Moderator: 
Ladies and gentlemen, good day, and welcome to the Ujjivan Small Finance Bank Limited Q2 
and H1 FY27 Earnings Conference Call, hosted by ICICI Securities Limited. As a reminder, all 
participant lines will be in the listen-only mode and there will be an opportunity for you to ask 
questions after the presentation concludes. Should you need assistance during the conference 
call, please signal an operator by pressing star then zero on your touch-tone phone. 
I now hand the conference over to Mr. Renish Bhuva from ICICI Securities Limited. Thank you, 
and over to you, sir. 
Renish Bhuva: 
Thank you, Rutuja. Hi. Good evening, everyone, and welcome to Ujjivan Small Finance Bank 
Q2 FY27 Earnings Call. On behalf of ICICI Securities, I would like to thank Ujjivan SFB 
management team for giving us the opportunity to host this call. 
Today, we have with us the entire top management team of Ujjivan represented by Ms. Carol 
Furtado, Whole-Time Director and Interim CEO; Mr. Balakrishna Kamath, CFO; Mr. Ashish 
Goel, Chief Credit Officer; Mr. Vibhas, Head, Micro Banking; Mr. Hitendra Jha, Head, Retail 
Liabilities, TASC and Third-Party Product; Mr. Pradeep, Head, Housing and Micro-Mortgage; 
Mr. Martin, Chief Operating Officer; Mr. Brajesh, Chief Risk Officer; Mr. Siddharth, Head, 
Investor Relations; and Mr. Gaurav Sah, Lead Investor Relations. 
I will now hand over the call to Carol ma'am for opening remarks, and then we'll open the floor 
for Q&A. Over to you, ma'am. 
Carol Furtado: 
Thank you, Renish. Good evening, and thank you all for joining us to discuss Ujjivan Small 
Finance Bank's Q2 FY27 Earnings Call. Please note, I will be referring to year-on-year 
comparisons with Q2 FY26 and quarter-on-quarter with Q1 FY27. 
I would like to start with a few important developments before delving into the quarter. Post our 
MD, Mr. Sanjeev Nautiyal's decision to take an early retirement due to health reasons, the NRC 
is actively engaged to ensure timely submission of the MD candidate to the regulator.  
Our growth in H1 FY27 has been built on strategic capacity creation and product evolution. This 
is matched with pristine asset quality outcomes. We remain well positioned with regards to 
people, technology, systems, and risk management to continue this growth momentum. 
Within the shareholders approved resolution at the AGM, we propose to raise equity capital of 
INR409 crores from QIBs by issuing shares on a preferential basis to marquee investors, 
International Finance Corporation, Bajaj Life Insurance, HDFC Life Insurance, and Aditya Birla 
Sun Life Insurance, subject to shareholder approval. Holding the RWA constant at September 
'26, the proposed capital raise would increase CRAR by approximately 1.2% from 20.69% on a 
pro forma basis.  
Since fundraise is being done at a premium to current BVPS, it will lead to accretion of INR0.8 
per share as of September '26. We remain nimble to the evolving needs of the bank. Thus, as

shared, we have enhanced our funding mix by increasing the securitization pool by INR500 
crores in October month. This will be NIM accretive and P&L neutral. 
Now coming to the operating environment. India's GDP, gross capital formation and high-
frequency indicators remain healthy and appear resilient to external shocks. Renewed conflict 
in the Middle East and increased volatility in global energy and freight prices are adding to 
inflationary pressures.  
In its latest MPC statement, the RBI raised its FY27 GDP growth forecast to 7.1%, while the 
committee increased the repo rate by 25 bps and shifted to calibrated tightening. A deficient 
Southwest monsoon and strong El Nino conditions pose risk to rural demand, while urban 
demand remained stable. 
Q2 of FY27 has demonstrated another quarter of strong growth anchored on well-rounded credit 
growth and stable margins. Along guided lines, in H1 of FY27, we have strengthened our 
distribution by adding 104 branches and 1,335 employees. We launched a well-curated brand 
campaign in September '26 with a new brand ambassador, Padma Shri Awardee, Mr. R. 
Madhavan.  
Ujjivan today has evolved significantly in terms of its scale, reach and breadth of offerings. The 
tagline, Nothing Small About Us, reflects the scale of Ujjivan's aspirations, reach and the breadth 
of financial solutions it offers. This campaign will be run across TV, print, and digital and is 
expected to reach around 35 crores viewers. Other institutional building spends on digital and 
technology have been set in motion and will reflect in H2. 
This quarter marked an important milestone as we crossed INR50,000 crores in deposits. Total 
deposits increased to INR50,643 crores, up 29.2% year-on-year with CASA at 26%. We 
continue to add customers and increase volumes across our various deposit offerings. We 
benefited from the downward repricing of deposits, which helped maintain the cost of funds at 
around 6.9%. Although no rate hikes were taken in Q2, the increase effective in Q1 would now 
start showing, and we expect the cost of funds to start moving upwards. 
In line with our strategy to expand services for depositors, we launched the ASBA facility in 
Q2. Going forward, we will focus on simplifying transactions, increasing awareness and 
adoption of newly introduced services and deepening engagement with customers. The gross 
loan book clocked robust growth and reached INR45,699 crores, up 32.1% year-on-year. This 
translates to 12.4% YTD growth and are on track to meet the full year guidance. 
The secured business lines continue to grow faster and now forms 52.1% of the loan book. The 
unsecured piece consisting of micro banking delivered healthy growth, reaching INR22,037 
crores. This portfolio has grown approximately 6% in the first half of FY27 and remains on track 
to deliver around 12% to 14% for the full year. 
Some key callouts for the quarter in micro banking. Collection efficiency remains strong with 
Bucket X collection efficiency at 99.7%, in line with Q1 outcome. New customer acquisition

increased sequentially with an addition of 2 lakh customers in Q2. Despite usual weather 
disruptions in July, August, September, we have delivered on healthy disbursements and 
collections. Going ahead, our endeavor is to make newly added branches come up the 
productivity curve. 
Our housing business is a key vertical for the bank that caters to the aspirations of our customer 
base. Affordable housing and micro mortgages combined crossed INR12,000 crores, up 38.1% 
year-on-year. This quarter, the affordable housing crossed an important milestone by crossing 
INR10,000 crores mark and reached INR10,056 crores. Portfolio quality remains stable with 
PAR and GNPA at 3.7% and 1.2%, respectively. The balance transfer out for Q2 was flat 
sequentially at 4.3%. We are targeting to preserve yields and are comfortable with the current 
growth levels. 
Micro mortgages growth remains strong. Loan book crossed INR2,000 crores, reaching 
INR2,031 crores, up 85.7% year-on-year. Portfolio quality continues to season at a comfortable 
pace with GNPA at 0.7%. The MSME business built upon the capacities created and product 
changes grew to INR3,871 crores, up 51.3% year-on-year. The new book reached INR3,000 
crores plus while maintaining GNPA of 0.5%. 
Gold loan continues to witness larger industry-wide tailwinds and grew to INR1,275 crores, up 
209.8% year-on-year. In H1, we have added 117 branches and plan to expand to a similar number 
of branches in H2. The disbursement LTVs are maintained below 78%. Agri banking grew to 
INR914 crores, up 79.2% year-on-year. 
As part of strategy, we operate in select locations with due importance to environmental factors. 
Portfolio in Karnataka is INR165 crores. Out of this, INR1.2 crores is eligible under the relief 
scheme and direct agri exposure in Maharashtra is nil. 2-wheeler loans grew to INR1,081 crores, 
up 64.8% year-on-year.  
We are geared up for the festive season and expect enhanced business momentum. The asset 
quality performance as measured across parameters remained steady. The slippage ratio is at 
1.6% of average gross loan book, while the credit cost came in at 0.7% of ATA. PCR continued 
to remain stable at 85% level. GNPA and NNPA remained healthy at 2.1% and 0.3%, 
respectively. Total write-off for the quarter was at INR59 crores. 
Financial performance. Robust asset growth translated into strong revenue momentum with total 
income reaching INR2,450 crores and NII rising 35% year-on-year to INR1,244 crores. 
Advances yield continues to be in comfortable zone and cost of funds remained largely stable, 
leading to net interest margin at 8.4%. Other income for the quarter increased at a healthy 17% 
sequentially. 
Operating expenses increased by 6% quarter-on-quarter, wherein employee expenses increased 
by 3% quarter-on-quarter and other opex by 10%. The increased opex was on account of planned 
investments in a comprehensive brand campaign and ongoing branch network expansion. This 
has resulted in an all-time high quarterly profit after tax of INR365 crores with ROA of 2.4%

and ROE of 19.7%. We are taking steps to optimize capital consumption and have seen CRAR 
improvement by 33 bps to 20.69% as of September '26. This is largely onetime, and we would 
resume consumption in a normalized run rate going forward. 
H2 outlook and guidance. Strong advanced growth in H1 will support interest and related income 
growth run rate. However, the change in policy rates and resultant pass-through will lead to 
higher interest expenses than planned. While opex towards institutional build-out will accelerate, 
we anticipate a slower pace as planned. Asset quality outcomes are also expected to be along 
delivered lines.  
Considering these outcomes, we could overshoot our guided ROA range. We remain vigilant of 
revised monetary stance, risk of global rates and supply chain disruptions, coupled with weather-
induced issues. Our high-frequency indicators across products for October remain in line with 
recent outcomes. 
IRDAI's notification is a consultation paper, and we await the final guidelines on the matter. We 
remain engaged with our insurance partners as well as through IBA channels. Since discussions 
with IRDAI are ongoing and submissions are due on October 25, it would be premature to 
elaborate further. However, we are closely watching the developments. 
Lastly, I would like to say that at Ujjivan, our strategic focus continues to be on diversified 
advances growth with shift towards secured assets, while we build the bank to provide Indians 
with the access to their financial aspirations. 
With that, I conclude my opening remarks and request the moderator to open the floor for 
questions. Thank you.

are included as per the SLBC document, out of INR2,400 crores in Karnataka, only INR15.1

the entire Maharashtra microfinance portfolio is INR1,682 crores. Out of that, agri-related loans, 
which qualifies as per SLBC is only INR18 crores, it is less than 1%.
